'''Emma Previato''' (November 29, 1952 – June 29, 2022) was an Italian–born American professor of mathematics at [[Boston University]].<ref name=ams>{{cite journal|last1=Donagi |first1=Ron |last2=Matsutani |first2=Shigeki |last3=Roubtsov |first3=Volodya |last4=Adams |first4=Malcolm R. |last5=Mumford |first5=David |last6=Glazebrook |first6=James |last7=Thompson |first7=Ben |last8=Jeffrey |first8=Lisa |title=Emma Previato|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|date=September 2023|volume=70|issue=8|pages=1243–1251|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/202308/rnoti-p1243.pdf|doi=10.1090/noti2763|doi-access=free}}</ref> Her research focused on [[algebraic geometry]] and [[partial differential equation]]s.

==Career==
Previato received her Ph.D. from [[Harvard University]] in 1983 under [[David Mumford]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=11731|title=Emma Previato}}</ref> She was a faculty member at [[Boston University]].<ref name=ams/> She was the author or co-author of nearly 100 research articles. She served as editor or co-editor of 6 books,<ref name=ams/> including ''Dictionary of Applied Math for Engineers and Scientists'' (2002, [[CRC Press]]).<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-1PMBQAAQBAJ | title=Dictionary of Applied Math for Engineers and Scientists | isbn=9781420037760 | last1=Previato | first1=Emma | date=29 October 2002 | publisher=CRC Press }}</ref>

Previato founded Boston University's chapters of the [[Mathematical Association of America]]<ref name=news /> and of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bu.edu/hic/profile/emma-previato/|title=Emma Previato|publisher=[[Boston University]]|work=Hariri Institute for Computing}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2003, she received the [[Mathematical Association of America]] Northeastern Section's Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics for her work in and out of the classroom, especially her mentoring of students.<ref name=news>{{cite web|location=Boston University News Releases|title=Boston University Professor to Receive Regional Distinguished Teacher of the Year Award|last=Menting|first=Ann|url=http://www.bu.edu/news/2003/04/20/boston-university-professor-to-receive-regional-distinguished-teacher-of-the-year-award/|access-date=Feb 9, 2015|date=Apr 20, 2003}}</ref>

In 2012, Previato became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |access-date=2015-02-09 |archive-date=2018-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Previato was born in [[Badia Polesine]] in 1952. She earned undergraduate and master's degrees from the [[University of Padua]] before beginning her PhD at Harvard.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Kielanowski |first1=Piotr |last2=Dobrogowska |first2=Alina |last3=Goldin |first3=Gerald |last4=Goliński |first4=Tomasz |contribution=In Memoriam: Emma Previato 1952–2022 |title=Geometric methods in physics XXXIX |year=2023|series=Trends in Mathematics|pages=5–6 | publisher=[[Birkhäuser]]|location=Cham|doi=10.1007/978-3-031-30284-8_2 |isbn=978-3-031-30283-1 }}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* Previato, Emma. Hyperelliptic quasiperiodic and soliton solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation]. ''[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]'' 52 (1985), no. 2, 329–377. {{doi|10.1215/S0012-7094-85-05218-4}}
* Adams, M. R.; Harnad, J.; Previato, E. Isospectral Hamiltonian flows in finite and infinite dimensions. I. Generalized Moser systems and moment maps into loop algebras. ''[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]]'' 117 (1988), no. 3, 451–500. {{doi|10.1007/BF01223376}}
* Eilbeck, J. C.; Enolski, V. Z.; Matsutani, S.; Ônishi, Y.; Previato, E. Abelian functions for trigonal curves of genus three. ''[[International Mathematics Research Notices]]'' 2008, no. 1, Art. ID rnm 140, 38 pp.
* {{cite book |last1=Kielanowski |first1=Piotr |last2=Odzijewicz |first2=Anatol |last3=Previato |first3=Emma |title=Geometric Methods in Physics XXXV: Workshop and Summer School, Bialowieza, Poland, June 26 - July 2, 2016 |series=[[Trends in Mathematics]] |publisher=Birkhäuser |date=2018-02-11 |isbn=978-3-319-63593-4 |edition=1st ed. 2018}}
